req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT be honoured (boundary ±1 outside range); (4) test missing status_code defaults to 302; (5) test non-redirect codes like 200 and 500 are ignored; (6) assert the Location header equals the supplied URL exactly. Each test is self-contained, uses Flask test_client with follow_redirects=False so we see the raw redirect response.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact_match
actions: Iterate over [301,302,303,307,308] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code matches the requested code exactly
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: all five required codes must be honoured
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact_match():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code={}'.format(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, 'Expected {} got {}'.format(code, r.status_code)
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact_match()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_boundary_301_not_300_not_302
actions: GET /redirect-to with status_code=301; verify it is not 300 and not 302
expected: Status code is exactly 301, not 300, not 302
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: catches off-by-one mutations on the 301 constant
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_boundary_301_not_300_not_302():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.status_code != 300
    assert r.status_code != 302

test_redirect_to_boundary_301_not_300_not_302()
